gaps.sentence: She is very ___ in modern art (INTEREST).
gaps.hint: how she feels: -ed; fixed pattern '___ in'
gaps.explanation: 'Interested in something' describes the person's feeling; 'interesting' describes the thing that causes it.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ of you to double-check the figures (SENSE).
gaps.explanation: 'It was sensible of you to do something' praises good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: The hospital provides ___ care around the clock (PERSON).
gaps.hint: adjective needed before the noun 'care'; beware the word meaning 'staff'
gaps.explanation: 'Personal care' uses the adjective 'personal'; 'personnel' is a noun meaning staff.

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: After the fire, the theatre had to be completely ___ (BUILD).
gaps.hint: build again after destruction (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rebuilt. The passive needs the past participle after 'had to be'.
